answer.rationale: The low-cost vendor's price already satisfies the 18% cost-cut mandate on its own (c2 documents that onboarding was quick and invoicing has been accurate, which reduces delivery-risk concerns tied to switching). The 94% utilization with no buffer means stability matters, but c2 indicates the vendor transition was previously fast and accurate. I want to verify c2 because the current decision hinges on whether that prior low-cost onboarding experience still applies — any issues with their invoicing accuracy or delivery reliability would change the calculus. I am not verifying c6 (multi-year volume pricing) or c4 (renegotiation leverage) because the mandate is already met by the quoted price; I don't need to chase additional margin. Renewing the incumbent would not hit the mandate; adding a second source would not reduce spend in this cycle; deferring would miss the 14-day window and likely force a month-to-month or auto-lapse.
